cards.q: What is a client-based Remote Access VPN?
cards.a: It is a per-user VPN where a software client such as Cisco AnyConnect builds an encrypted tunnel into the enterprise from anywhere over the Internet, giving the user full network access and strong corporate control.

cards.q: What is the difference between client-based and clientless remote access?
cards.a: Client-based requires a software client and gives full network access with strong control, while clientless uses only a browser portal to reach specific internal applications with no install.

cards.q: What are the two client-based transport options and their ports?
cards.a: IPsec RA uses IKE over UDP 500/4500 and provides strong control, while SSL/AnyConnect rides TLS on TCP 443 (with DTLS on UDP 443) and is firewall-friendly.

cards.q: What is the difference between full-tunnel and split-tunnel?
cards.a: Full-tunnel sends all client traffic through the headend for security and filtering but increases load, while split-tunnel sends only corporate subnets through the VPN and lets local Internet traffic go direct for better performance.

cards.q: What authentication and security mechanisms are used for remote access VPN?
cards.a: User authentication via AAA (RADIUS/LDAP), multi-factor authentication with tokens or certificates, AnyConnect endpoint posture assessment, and group policies that define per-user access and split/full tunneling.

cards.q: What is the role of DTLS in AnyConnect?
cards.a: DTLS runs on UDP 443 and provides lower latency than TLS for real-time, latency-sensitive applications such as voice and video over the AnyConnect tunnel.

cards.q: Which devices typically act as the remote access VPN headend?
cards.a: The headend is usually an ASA, ASAv, ISR router, or FTD firewall terminating the AnyConnect or IPsec client sessions.

cards.q: Which commands verify remote access VPN sessions?
cards.a: show vpn-sessiondb anyconnect, show vpn-sessiondb ikev2, show vpn-sessiondb summary, show tunnel-group, and show crypto ikev2 sa.

cards.q: A client can establish an IPsec RA tunnel but has no full access to the network; what is likely wrong?
cards.a: The group policy is probably set for split-tunnel, so only corporate subnets are routed through the VPN; check split-tunnel-policy and the split-tunnel ACL in the group policy.

cards.q: What is the key exam distinction between client-based and clientless remote access?
cards.a: Client-based uses a software client such as AnyConnect with full network access and strong control, while clientless is browser-only app access with no install.

cards.q: What is the remote access VPN quick-review summary?
cards.a: Client-based RA VPN uses a software client (AnyConnect) to build an IPsec (UDP 500/4500) or SSL/DTLS (TCP/UDP 443) tunnel to an ASA/ISR headend, supports full or split tunneling, and is secured with AAA, MFA, certificates, posture, and group policies.
